parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no documented police targeting, border screening, facility ban or custody rule; foreign documents are not shown to be a problem. Strong recent institutional positives: sodomy decriminalised in 2022 via a trans activist's constitutional challenge, and a 2023 high court ruling that orientation discrimination is unconstitutional; a pro-LGBT PM; small Pride and Trans Day of Remembrance vigils. Against: official and religious hostility (the state questioning LGBT migration; fundamentalist rhetoric encouraging discrimination), an employment act omitting gender identity, and one documented anti-trans attack (2018) whose attacker got a fine and no jail — a lenient-sentence signal, but single, dated, prosecuted, not a pattern. No trans-specific violence rate or visitor-facing incident is documented; border, facilities, custody and care are open questions rather than exposures. It lacks the documented visitor-facing remedy and acceptance of the 0.65 tier, but also lacks the repeated visitor-facing harms of the 0.55 tier.
